Subject: Onramp playline & invoicing gate — Meditech MAP

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out the evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria, and the billing path for the AWS private-offer option. High-level ask: can your procurement team confirm the PO cadence and whether Meditech prefers marketplace-commit (AWS Private Offer) or a direct invoice to your AP team once contracts are signed?

Key milestones in the attached MAP (Meditech_MAP_v1.pdf):
- Week 0–2: SSO onboarding & service account verification (test tenant provided by Meditech)
- Week 2–4: Acceptance run of 3 production-like prompts and latency/cost verification
- Week 4: Sign SOW and activate AWS private offer (if chosen)
- Week 4–6: Billing gate — invoice issued after SOW signature OR trigger via marketplace commit (we can match whichever you prefer)

Attachments included: Meditech_MAP_v1.pdf, SOW-draft.docx (editable)

Open items for your team:
1) Procurement contact for PO routing (name + email + invoicing preference)
2) Any required vendor fields (tax id, billing address, PO reference)
3) SSO test account window and a point of contact for the acceptance run

If you prefer, we can run the acceptance tests in parallel with legal review so the activation happens faster once the SOW is signed.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa (CS) and Jonas (solutions) to help with the acceptance checklist.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia — looping in the acceptance checklist as requested and a short note on billing choices.

Acceptance checklist (summary):
- SSO connection validated (SAML assertion + test user login)
- Sample inference run (3 workload prompts) with latency & token-cost snapshot attached
- KV/prefix caching verification for the 3 prompt families
- Security scan smoke test (run by Meditech infra)

We’ve uploaded a simple checklist and example test data here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cmeditech-map (please let me know if access is blocked).

Quick billing tradeoffs:
- Marketplace private-offer (AWS) — faster activation for cloud-native procurement teams, billing goes through marketplace; simpler for customers who want cloud billing consolidation.
- Direct invoice (Redwood invoice to Meditech AP) — better for customers who need standard vendor terms (Net 30) and purchase-order controls. Either option is fine; we typically map the final choice to how finance prefers to recognize spend.

Michael — can you confirm if you want the SOW to include a PO reference and your preferred net terms? If you want, I can update the SOW and send a DocuSign link to speed signature. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/67890

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
